# Theme tokens

Hosts send renderers a theme of design tokens; renderers style themselves with them, so a renderer matches whatever
host shows it. This is token set version `0`: every token below is always defined
(`resolveThemeTokens` fills any a host omits with these defaults). CSS reads each as `--projections-<name>`.

Version of the theme token set. Hosts send `theme.version`; renderers can
rely on every token of this version being defined (`resolveThemeTokens`
fills any a host omits with these defaults).
/
export const themeTokenSetVersion = 0 as const

type Pair = readonly [light: string, dark: string]
const same = (value: string): Pair => [value, value]

/**
Token set 1, with light and dark defaults: the Projector theme of the default
UI (screen-white and graphite neutrals, the cyan lens for focus and selection). Names are kebab-case; CSS reads
them as `--projections-<name>` after `applyEnvironment`.

- `color-*` surfaces: `bg` (canvas), `bg-subtle`, `bg-inset` (recessed
  wells), `bg-overlay` (popovers, floating panels); text `fg`, `fg-muted`,
  `fg-subtle`, `fg-on-emphasis` (text on emphasis fills).
- Stacked surfaces, in elevation order with visible steps in both modes:
  `surface-canvas` (the stage behind cards) < `surface-raised` (a card) <
  `surface-header` (a header band in a card) and `surface-inset` (a recessed
  column such as a line-number gutter, or room with nothing in it);
  `color-divider` separates any two of them at 3:1 or more against both, as a
  card's edge or a band's rule. Quieter rules between rows keep `border`.
- Change regions: a tinted area always has a defining edge, never a fill
  alone. `-muted` is the fill and `-border` the edge in the same hue, at 3:1
  or more against the raised surface and the canvas.
- Change colors for `added`, `removed`, `modified` and `moved`: the base
  color (text and strokes), `-muted` (subtle fills) and `-emphasis` (strong
  fills behind `fg-on-emphasis` text), and `-highlight`: stronger than
  `-muted` but still drawn behind plain `fg` text, for word-level changes.
- `color-highlight`: a neutral highlight behind plain `fg` text, for hover
  emphasis and find matches.
- `chart-1` … `chart-16`: a categorical palette of sixteen distinct hues
  (blue, teal, pink, lime, purple, cyan, indigo, sky, orange, green,
  red, violet, emerald, rose, amber, citron) calibrated to the theme: muted
  (chroma capped, well under the change colors, so change status always
  stands out), in one narrow lightness band, each at least 3:1 against
  `color-bg`. Generated by `scripts/palette.mjs`. `chart-1` … `chart-8`
  avoid the change hues (green, red, amber, violet), so categories don't
  read as added, removed, modified or moved. None is gray: renderers keep
  the neutral `color-border-emphasis` for "other".
- Type scale `font-size-xs` … `font-size-xl`, weights, line heights; spacing
  `space-1` … `space-8`; radii; border widths; shadows; control heights;
  focus ring; label (badge) metrics.
- `icon-<name>`: the icon vocabulary (`iconNames`), each an SVG data URL a
  renderer draws as a mask in `currentColor`; Lucide by default, and a host
  may map them to its own design system's icons (see `icons.ts`). The badge
  icons are the SDK's own glyphs, one stroke, centred on their disc, in
  every host.
- Optional layout tokens (`optionalThemeTokenNames`), which have no default: a renderer reads one with its own
  value as the fallback, `var(--projections-stage-inset, 12px)`, so hosts that don't send it see no change.
  `stage-inset` is the space between the frame's edges and the content a renderer lays out on its stage (its cards,
  tables or fitted canvas), the same on all four sides, so a card or table sits evenly in the frame; the renderer
  kit's stage padding (`pk-stage`) is it, else 12px. A host that lines that content up with its page's own column
  sends it, and extends the frame past the column by the same amount so rings at the edges still show.
  `stage-inset-top` is the space between the frame's top edge and the content that the host overlays (such as a
  pane's label chip): a host that does sends it, so the content starts at least that far down while the renderer's
  background still reaches under it; the kit's stage padding is at its top the larger of the two.
  `stage-max-height` (`px`, or `vh` of the host's window) caps a content-sized stage that pans and zooms: a host
  that lays frames in its scrolling page sends it, and such a stage then pans by dragging, leaving the wheel to the page.

## Icons

The icon vocabulary: semantic names a renderer asks for, never a specific
glyph. Each is a theme token, `icon-<name>`, whose value is a CSS image
(an SVG data URL) that renderers draw as a mask in `currentColor`, so its
shape comes from the host and its color from the text beside it. An icon
never carries meaning alone: it always accompanies its word.

- Changes: `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `renamed`, `moved`.
- Severity: `warning`, `error`, `breaking`, `info`, `unknown`.
- Compatibility and versions: `additive`, `compatible`, `upgraded`,
  `downgraded`, `changed` (changed either way).
- Policy and coverage: `enforced`, `unenforced`, `include`, `exclude`,
  `visible`, `hidden`, `expand`, `collapse`, `rescoped` (a scope changed
  either way), `settings`, `agent`.
- Planned actions: `replace`, `redeploy`, `import`, `read`, `blocked`.
- Volatile data: `varied`, a volatile value (one an extraction declares may
  vary between runs) that changed beyond its tolerance. Neutral, never a
  change kind: draw it in the text color beside the change's own status.
  `generated`, a value an extractor generated from a recorded basis (a
  summary a language model wrote, say): the quiet mark beside every
  generated field's name. Neutral, never a change kind.
- Subjects, what a section holds, beside its title: `host` (the nodes a
  system runs on), `policy`, `workload`, `credential`, `process`, `file`,
  `network`, `module` (a loadable extension, such as a kernel module),
  `bytecode` (a loaded program, such as BPF), `namespace` (an isolation
  boundary or mount), `application` (user-space programs) and `other`.
- Projection parts: `extractor`, `comparator`, `renderer`. Their own
  drawings, not Lucide's: a dot is the extraction, the same size in all
  three; strokes converge on it (extract), two dots sit either side of a
  dashed divider (compare), and strokes leave it (render).

The defaults are the default UI's icons, drawn in the text color beside them. Light and dark are the same image.
